summary: Stale role enforcement after SCIM group change due to identity-proxy token cache in private VPC
description:
Issue summary: BrightForms reported that after removing a user from their 'platform-admins' SCIM group the user retained admin privileges for ~12-20 minutes. This occurs on their Private VPC deployment and affects administrative flows (console role toggle, admin-only ML endpoints).

Impact: Affected customer admin users continued to see admin-only routes succeed (400+ admin actions observed in audit logs) even after SCIM shows the user removed. This is causing customer confusion and potential security exposure. No service-wide outage; scoped to BrightForms private deployment.

Background: BrightForms uses SCIM provisioning from their IdP (Okta) into Redwood's SCIM API. They use service account JWTs for automation with long-lived tokens (~1h). Identity-proxy is configured in front of private control plane and applies RBAC decisions using a short-lived introspection cache (~15m TTL).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In IdP (Okta), remove user alice@brightforms.com from SCIM group 'platform-admins'
2) Confirm SCIM API shows membership removed (GET /scim/Groups/:id returns no member alice)
3) On customer side, perform an admin-only action via service account (e.g., admin rollout or console user list) using an existing JWT issued 20 minutes prior
4) Observe that action succeeds despite SCIM removal
5) Clear identity-proxy cache or wait ~15 minutes, retry action and observe expected 403
logs: 2026-03-12T10:02:11Z identity-proxy INFO request=abcd123 token_sub=svc-automation-42 cache=HIT decision=allow
2026-03-12T10:02:12Z scim-provisioner INFO group_update Group=platform-admins removed=alice@brightforms.com event_id=scim-evt-987
2026-03-12T10:15:00Z identity-proxy WARN request=efgh456 token_sub=alice@brightforms.com cache=HIT decision=allow (expected deny)
2026-03-12T10:28:05Z admin-console INFO audit user=alice@brightforms.com action=delete_model model_id=m-21 result=success
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Token introspection/cache TTL causing stale role decisions after SCIM changes.
Confirmed: authz-cache keyed by token 'sub' stores resolved role set and is not being invalidated on SCIM webhook events for group membership changes.

Observed mismatch in identity keys: SCIM membership removal event references 'userName' (alice@brightforms.com) while cached key used 'sub' from service tokens (svc-automation-42). For human users the subject is email; for service tokens it is service-id; our cache invalidation currently only listens for userName -> sub mapping updates in certain flows, so service-account-linked roles remain cached until TTL expires.

Replication: In staging we reproduced by removing user from SCIM group and verifying cache invalidation only occurs after explicit cache flush or TTL expiry. Adding a patch to emit cache-invalidate events from scim-provisioner triggers immediate invalidation.
Correlated: No evidence of token replay or duplicate tokens; this is strictly an authorization cache invalidation gap after provisioning events.
resolution: Workaround (customer-facing): Instruct BrightForms to rotate the service JWT (short-term) or use Admin Console 'Invalidate auth cache' button if available. We provided CLI steps to call /admin/cache/invalidate?sub=svc-automation-42 (private control plane endpoint) with proof-of-possession headers.
Temporary mitigation (platform): Manually triggered cache flush for BrightForms' identity namespace at 2026-03-12T11:00Z; observed subsequent admin action returned 403 as expected.

Planned fix: Engineering to update scim-provisioner to publish explicit cache-invalidation events for both userName and any linked service 'sub' identifiers when group membership changes. Also add a mapping reconciliation job that detects stale cached roles vs SCIM authoritative state and invalidates caches proactively. Target PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/482
Post-action: Will add a telemetry alert to detect >5 minute divergence between SCIM state and authz cache for any customer in private tier.
